name: CDM collateral prototype
description: Local prototype architecture for CDM-based initial-margin management with tokenized collateral on Hyperledger Besu.

metadata.status: partially built: the IM and VM margin call lifecycles (flow-im-margin-call-pledge, flow-vm-margin-call-transfer, flow-return), flow-default-enforcement, flow-oracle-update and flow-revaluation-top-up run live on the contracts, ledger gateway, collateral service, oracle service (default notices and prices), CDM payload store and console (task-e2e-wiring, task-e2e-remaining-flows)

nodes.name: Development host

Java and Node.js services run on the host; the Besu nodes run in Docker Compose.

metadata.alternative: Windows 11 with WSL2 and Docker Desktop

nodes.name: Participant stack
nodes.description: Per-participant deployment (ADR wp-adr-per-participant-services): each simulated participant runs its own party console, collateral workflow service, workflow store, ledger gateway and keystore, holding only its own books and its own signing key, and connected to its own Besu validator node. N stacks run side by side; the oracle service, mock market data and contracts are shared.

metadata.instances: N, one per participant (pledgor, secured party, market operator)
metadata.isolation: own process, own SQLite file, own key; no shared database

nodes.name: CDM collateral prototype
nodes.description: Prototype that illustrates CDM-based initial-margin management with tokenized collateral segregated by a smart contract on a local Besu network. Nothing is deployed outside the developer machine.

nodes.name: Collateral workflow service
nodes.description: Off-chain margin workflow (ASR concept-asr-onchain-call-state: negotiation and CDM content off-chain, call state on-chain), one instance per participant: holds that party's CDM agreements (ISDA IM CSA / CTA-SA elections, eligibility schedule), checks eligibility and haircuts with CDM functions, runs the margin call lifecycle (issue, respond, dispute, propose, decide, settle) that CDM 7.7.0 does not provide (finding F2) with the local CDM extension (cdm-ext), and sends its own party's movement instructions to its ledger gateway. Each lifecycle step is one CDM MarginCallInstruction serialised to canonical Rune JSON and hashed with keccak-256; the service writes the document to the CDM payload store and the hash goes on-chain (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier). It reads the counterparty's steps from the chain and the store, not from the counterparty's instance (the one direct link between the two instances is the trade snapshot exchange of flow-reconciliation, service-to-counterparty-service), and folds every step in chain order into one cumulative, validated MarginCallState per call (CDM Create_MarginCallState); both parties' folds converge to an identical state. It relays its gateway's event stream to its console over Server-Sent Events.

metadata.cdm-binding: CDM 7.7.0 Java (org.finos.cdm:cdm-java) and the local extension cdmx generated to Java (cdm-ext), ADR wp-adr-java-cdm-stack

nodes.name: CDM 7.7.0 object model
nodes.description: FINOS Common Domain Model release 7.7.0 (commit 1c97666, Java distribution) as the canonical data layer (ASR concept-asr-cdm-data-layer): LegalAgreement with CSA IM / CTA elections, EligibleCollateralSpecification, MarginCallIssuance / MarginCallResponse, CollateralPortfolio. Extended locally (cdm-ext, namespaces cdmx.*: margin call lifecycle, events, transfers) and with on-chain asset identity (ASR concept-asr-onchain-asset-identity, finding B1).

nodes.name: Workflow store
nodes.description: One SQLite file per participant holding that party's agreements, margin calls and responses, disputes, movement instructions, collateral balances and the asset registry that maps ISIN/CUSIP and DTI to network and token contract.

nodes.name: CDM payload store
nodes.description: Content-addressed store for the CDM document of every margin call lifecycle step (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier). A document is stored under its keccak-256 hash, which is also the cdmHash the margin call contract records for that step: the hash is the retrieval key and the integrity check (the store rejects a body that does not hash to its key, and a reader recomputes the hash). Each document carries a reader allowlist of the call's two counterparty addresses. Callers authenticate with a per-party bearer token that the store resolves to the party's address; it fails closed with no tokens configured. One shared instance serves all participants.

metadata.authentication: per-party bearer token (shared secret, PARTY_TOKENS / STORE_TOKEN)
metadata.production: mutual TLS or signed requests; a shared content-addressed store or IPFS with access control, or per-party stores

nodes.name: Oracle service
nodes.description: Off-chain oracle endpoints, shared, run by the market data operator. Reads price / NAV and rating data from the mock market data source, serves it to every participant's collateral service for valuation and eligibility, and publishes signed updates on-chain through the operator's ledger gateway. Also relays a default notice from the secured party to the on-chain default feed.

nodes.name: Mock market data source
nodes.description: Local JSON files standing in for NAV, price and rating providers (in the GDF/ISDA sandbox: Kaiko, Redstone, Moody's).

nodes.name: Ledger gateway
nodes.description: Ledger-neutral interface (ASR concept-asr-ledger-neutrality, ADR wp-adr-prototype-ledgers): one instance per participant: accepts its participant's movement instructions (and, for the operator, oracle updates), signs with that participant's key only and submits transactions to the ledger, waits for finality, serves a call's lifecycle steps in chain order with their cdmHash, and pushes chain events to the collateral service over Server-Sent Events from one eth_subscribe subscription on its Besu node. Besu adapter first; a Canton adapter is the second target.

nodes.name: Development keystore
nodes.description: Per participant: the private key of that participant's test account only (pledgor, secured party, or for the market operator the oracle publisher and contract admin keys). Development keys only.

nodes.name: Besu local network
nodes.description: Hyperledger Besu network in Docker Compose with QBFT consensus: four validator nodes, one per default participant (market operator, BANK-A, BANK-B, BANK-C), each participant's gateway connected to its own node (ADR wp-adr-per-participant-services). Deterministic finality per block (ASR concept-asr-settlement-finality); blocks continue with one node down. Stands in for a permissioned network such as DTCC's private Besu network.

metadata.consensus: QBFT, four validators, one node per participant

nodes.name: Tokenized collateral contracts
nodes.description: ERC-20 test tokens with transfer restrictions standing in for a tokenized money market fund and a tokenized US Treasury. Each token records its ISIN/CUSIP and DTI as metadata (ASR concept-asr-onchain-asset-identity).

nodes.name: Collateral control contract
nodes.description: Smart contract that holds pledged initial margin (ADR wp-adr-im-segregation). States per pledge: pledged, returned, enforced. Pledge: pledgor transfers tokens in, only against an agreed call whose collateral proposal the secured party accepted, only the accepted assets, and up to the agreed amount; the call is then marked settled. Return: needs approval by both parties or by the secured party. Enforce: secured party only, after the default feed reports a default. No other movement is possible.

nodes.name: Margin call contract
nodes.description: Records each margin call on-chain (ASR concept-asr-onchain-call-state, ADR wp-adr-margin-call-state-onchain): ID, agreement, caller and called party, called, agreed and disputed amounts, settlement deadline, call state (issued, agreed, partially agreed, disputed, settled), collateral proposal state (proposed, accepted, rejected) with the proposed assets and quantities, and for every lifecycle step the keccak-256 cdmHash of its CDM document, emitted on the step's event (CallIssued, CallAnswered, CollateralProposed, ProposalDecided, CallSettled; ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier). The document itself is in the CDM payload store. The caller's key issues and accepts or rejects a proposal; the called party's key responds and proposes. Read by the collateral control contract before a pledge. Every node can read it (assumption nw-assumption-besu-visibility).

nodes.name: Oracle feed contract
nodes.description: On-chain store of the latest price / NAV, rating and default status per asset and counterparty, written only by the oracle publisher account and read by the collateral control contract.

nodes.name: Portfolio reconciliation contract
nodes.description: On-chain record of portfolio reconciliation (flow-reconciliation, gap G35): the hash of each party's trade snapshot and the hash of the result each party computed from the two snapshots. A run is Agreed when the two result hashes match. No trade data is on-chain. Separate from the collateral control contract, which is close to the EIP-170 size limit (wp-adr-reconciliation-scope).

nodes.name: Repo settlement contract
nodes.description: Term repos under the GMRA (flow-repo-purchase-repurchase): the seller books the trade's hash and amounts, the buyer affirms the same hash, and the purchase and the repurchase each settle delivery versus payment when the second party instructs with the same CDM settlement hash, both legs in one transaction. No dates are checked on-chain; each service holds a business date. Separate from the collateral control contract, which is close to the EIP-170 size limit (wp-adr-repo-purchase-repurchase).

relationships.description: All prototype components run on one development host (a codespace or the Windows machine).
Components of the prototype system.
Components that run once per participant.
The collateral service is built on the CDM object model.
Smart contracts deployed on the local Besu network.
Pledgor operations responds to margin calls and approves returns in its party console instance.
Secured party operations issues margin calls, approves returns and declares defaults in its party console instance.
Market data operator changes mock NAV, prices and ratings in its party console instance.

Calls its own participant's workflow REST API for agreements, calls, responses, returns, defaults and balances; subscribes to the service's Server-Sent Events stream (/api/v1/events) for chain-event updates instead of polling.
Market operator console edits mock market data through the oracle service.
Reads token balances and pledge state for display.
Drives N console instances in parallel browser contexts.
Asserts on-chain state after each flow.

Writes the CDM document of each step it takes under its keccak-256 hash, with both counterparties on the reader allowlist; reads the counterparty's step documents by the cdmHash recorded on-chain and verifies keccak256(document) equals that hash before folding it. Authenticated with its own party's bearer token. This is the only path by which CDM content passes between the parties (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier).
Reads and writes agreements, calls, instructions, balances and the asset registry.
Requests prices / NAV and ratings for valuation, haircuts and eligibility; forwards default notices.
Reads and, on operator request, updates mock NAV, price and rating data.

Submits its own participant's ledger instructions, each with the cdmHash of the step's CDM document: issue, respond, propose, decide, and settle (IM pledge, VM transfer, return release or transfer back); enforce. Reads a call's lifecycle steps in chain order with their cdmHash (/ledger/v1/calls/{id}/steps) as the input to its fold. Reads oracle feed prices, pledged quantities and settlement history (CallSettled, Enforced) for the revaluation.

Sends this party's trade snapshot (a CDM PortfolioSnapshot as Rune JSON) to the counterparty's workflow service and receives the counterparty's in return (flow-reconciliation). Each side checks the snapshot it receives against the hash the other committed on-chain. No other step crosses between the two instances.
Publishes price and default updates for the on-chain feed through the market operator's gateway instance.
Loads the signing key of its own participant.
Submits signed transactions and reads state over JSON-RPC on its own participant's Besu node.
Subscribes to contract events and new blocks on its own participant's Besu node.

Pushes chain events (lifecycle steps with their cdmHash, pledges, transfers, returns, enforcements) to its own participant's workflow service over a Server-Sent Events stream that the service holds open and reconnects; the service relays each event to its console.
Moves pledged tokens with ERC-20 transferFrom / transfer (EVM call).
Checks that the pledge matches an agreed call, its accepted collateral proposal and the agreed amount, then marks the call settled with the settle step's cdmHash (EVM call).
Reads default status (and, for valuation checks, price) before enforcement (EVM call).

flows.name: Initial margin call, collateral proposal and on-chain pledge
flows.description: The secured party calls initial margin and records the call on-chain; the pledgor agrees in full or in part (a disputed part is recorded but resolved off-chain) and proposes collateral; the secured party checks the proposal against its own eligibility schedule and accepts or rejects it on-chain; the pledgor pledges the accepted assets, which the collateral control contract accepts only against the agreed call and accepted proposal. Each step's CDM document goes to the CDM payload store under its keccak-256 hash and the hash goes on-chain; each party reads the other's steps from the chain and the store, verifies them and folds them into an identical MarginCallState (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier).

transitions.description: Secured party issues an IM call under the agreement in its console.
Secured party console submits the call to the secured party's workflow service.

Secured party's service builds the issue step (CDM MarginCallInstruction, canonical Rune JSON), hashes it with keccak-256 and writes it to the payload store under that hash, with both counterparties on the reader allowlist.
Secured party's service sends the call (amount, deadline, cdmHash) to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the call in the margin call contract, signed with the secured party key (call state: issued; the CallIssued event carries the cdmHash).
The pledgor's gateway receives the CallIssued event from its own Besu node over its eth_subscribe subscription.
The pledgor's gateway pushes the event to the pledgor's service over Server-Sent Events; the service relays it to its console.
Pledgor's service reads the call's lifecycle steps in chain order, each with its cdmHash.
Pledgor's service fetches the issue document by its cdmHash, verifies keccak256(document) equals the on-chain hash, and folds it into its MarginCallState (Create_MarginCallState).
Pledgor responds in its console (agree, partially agree or dispute) and proposes collateral: one or more tokens and quantities.
Pledgor console submits the response and the collateral proposal to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service fetches NAV / prices and ratings for the proposed tokens.
Pledgor's service pre-checks eligibility and haircuts against the CDM eligibility schedule and records the response and proposal in its own store.
Pledgor's service writes the response and proposal step documents to the payload store under their keccak-256 hashes.
Pledgor's service sends the response (agreed and disputed amounts) and the proposal (assets, quantities), each with its cdmHash, to its gateway.

Pledgor's gateway records the response and the proposal in the margin call contract, signed with the pledgor key (proposal state: proposed; the CallAnswered and CollateralProposed events carry the cdmHashes).

Secured party's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, reads the new steps from its gateway, fetches the response and proposal documents by cdmHash, verifies them and folds them into its MarginCallState.
Secured party's service values the proposed tokens.
Secured party's service checks eligibility, haircuts and concentration limits against its own copy of the CDM eligibility schedule and records the result.
Secured party accepts or rejects the proposal in its console; a rejection sends the pledgor back to step 10 with a new proposal.
Secured party console submits the decision to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service writes the decision step document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Secured party's service sends the decision with its cdmHash to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the decision in the margin call contract, signed with the secured party key (proposal state: accepted; the ProposalDecided event carries the cdmHash).
Pledgor's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, fetches the decision document by cdmHash, verifies it and folds it.
Pledgor's service writes the settle step document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Pledgor's service sends a pledge instruction for every accepted asset, with the settle step's cdmHash, to its gateway.
Pledgor's gateway approves each accepted token and submits pledge(callId, proposalId, cdmHash), signed with the pledgor key.

Control contract checks the pledge against the agreed call, the accepted proposal and the agreed amount, then marks the call settled with the settle cdmHash (CallSettled); a disputed amount stays open on the call.
Contract pulls each accepted token from the pledgor's account into escrow.
Both parties' gateways receive the pledge and settlement events in finalized blocks.

Each gateway pushes the events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; each service fetches, verifies and folds the settle document, and both services hold an identical MarginCallState (equal keccak stateHash).
Both consoles, updated through the services' event streams, show the settled pledge, the new balance and any disputed amount.

flows.name: Variation margin call and title transfer
flows.description: The secured party calls variation margin and records the call on-chain; the pledgor agrees in full or in part and proposes cash or tokens; the secured party accepts or rejects the proposal on-chain; the pledgor transfers title to the accepted assets, which the collateral control contract accepts only against the agreed VM call and accepted proposal (settleByTransfer). Steps 1-25 are those of flow-im-margin-call-pledge with a VM call; settlement moves title instead of pledging into escrow. Each step is anchored by its cdmHash and its CDM document is in the CDM payload store (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier).

transitions.description: Secured party issues a VM call (title transfer) under the agreement in its console.
Secured party console submits the call to the secured party's workflow service.

Secured party's service builds the issue step (CDM MarginCallInstruction for a VM call, canonical Rune JSON), hashes it with keccak-256 and writes it to the payload store under that hash, with both counterparties on the reader allowlist.
Secured party's service sends the call (amount, deadline, cdmHash) to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the call in the margin call contract, signed with the secured party key (call state: issued; the CallIssued event carries the cdmHash).
The pledgor's gateway receives the CallIssued event from its own Besu node over its eth_subscribe subscription.
The pledgor's gateway pushes the event to the pledgor's service over Server-Sent Events; the service relays it to its console.
Pledgor's service reads the call's lifecycle steps in chain order, each with its cdmHash.
Pledgor's service fetches the issue document by its cdmHash, verifies keccak256(document) equals the on-chain hash, and folds it into its MarginCallState (Create_MarginCallState).
Pledgor responds in its console (agree, partially agree or dispute) and proposes cash or tokens to deliver, e.g. tUSD.
Pledgor console submits the response and the collateral proposal to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service fetches NAV / prices and ratings for the proposed tokens.
Pledgor's service pre-checks eligibility and haircuts against the CDM eligibility schedule and records the response and proposal in its own store.
Pledgor's service writes the response and proposal step documents to the payload store under their keccak-256 hashes.
Pledgor's service sends the response (agreed and disputed amounts) and the proposal (assets, quantities), each with its cdmHash, to its gateway.

Pledgor's gateway records the response and the proposal in the margin call contract, signed with the pledgor key (proposal state: proposed; the CallAnswered and CollateralProposed events carry the cdmHashes).

Secured party's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, reads the new steps from its gateway, fetches the response and proposal documents by cdmHash, verifies them and folds them into its MarginCallState.
Secured party's service values the proposed tokens.
Secured party's service checks eligibility, haircuts and concentration limits against its own copy of the CDM eligibility schedule and records the result.
Secured party accepts or rejects the proposal in its console; a rejection sends the pledgor back to step 10 with a new proposal.
Secured party console submits the decision to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service writes the decision step document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Secured party's service sends the decision with its cdmHash to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the decision in the margin call contract, signed with the secured party key (proposal state: accepted; the ProposalDecided event carries the cdmHash).
Pledgor's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, fetches the decision document by cdmHash, verifies it and folds it.
Pledgor's service writes the settle step document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Pledgor's service sends a transfer instruction for the accepted proposal, with the settle step's cdmHash, to its gateway.
Pledgor's gateway approves each accepted token and submits settleByTransfer(callId, proposalId, cdmHash), signed with the pledgor key.
Control contract checks that the call is a VM call, agreed or partially agreed, and that the proposal is accepted, then marks the call settled with the settle cdmHash (CallSettled).
Contract moves title to each accepted token directly from the deliverer's account to the receiver's account (no escrow) and emits Transferred.
Both parties' gateways receive the transfer and settlement events in finalized blocks.
Each gateway pushes the events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; each service fetches, verifies and folds the settle document.
Both consoles, updated through the services' event streams, show the settled VM call, both parties' new balances and any disputed amount.

flows.name: Oracle price and rating update
flows.description: The oracle service publishes current prices from its mock market data to the on-chain feed through the market operator's gateway, on request and whenever the operator edits a price; each party reads the feed from its own node. Ratings stay in the oracle's mock market data off-chain: the oracle feed contract stores prices and default status only.

transitions.description: Oracle reads the mock price and rating of each token (prices start from the values on the feed).
Oracle sends the price update (token address, price scaled by 1e8) to the market operator's gateway.
Operator's gateway writes the price to the oracle feed contract (publishPrice) with the oracle publisher key; other gateways refuse feed writes.

flows.name: Collateral revaluation and top-up call
flows.description: The market operator lowers the price of a pledged token in the operator console; the oracle publishes it to the feed. The secured party revalues the pledged IM at the feed prices after haircuts against the outstanding IM from settled calls, sees a shortfall and issues a top-up IM call (minimum transfer amount USD 500,000, rounded up to USD 10,000), which then follows the IM call flow. A top-up does not add to the requirement (wp-adr-revaluation-outstanding-im-from-calls).

transitions.description: Market operator edits the price of a token in the operator console (#/live/operator).
Operator console sends the new mock price (PUT /oracle/v1/market-data/{symbol}).
Oracle publishes the new price to the on-chain feed through the operator gateway before keeping it.
Oracle updates the mock market data.

Secured party service revalues (GET /api/v1/revaluation): pledged quantities at the feed prices after haircuts against the outstanding IM from calls settled since the last enforcement, top-ups excluded.
Secured party console shows the shortfall and the top-up amount and issues the top-up IM call, which follows flow-im-margin-call-pledge.

flows.name: Return of initial margin
flows.description: The pledgor calls for the return of excess initial margin; the return call is recorded on-chain; the secured party agrees it through the response step and releases the escrowed tokens (issue, respond, settle). Each step is anchored by its cdmHash and its CDM document is in the CDM payload store (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier).

transitions.description: Pledgor requests a return of excess initial margin in its console.
Pledgor console submits the request to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service writes the return call's CDM document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Pledgor's service sends the return call (amount, cdmHash) to its gateway.
Pledgor's gateway records the return call in the margin call contract, signed with the pledgor key.
Secured party's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, fetches the return call document by cdmHash, verifies it and folds it into its MarginCallState.
Secured party agrees the return in its console.
Secured party console submits the agreement to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service writes the response and settle step documents to the payload store under their keccak-256 hashes.
Secured party's service sends the response and the release instruction, each with its cdmHash, to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the response and submits returnCollateral(callId, assets, cdmHash), signed with the secured party key.
Control contract checks the agreed return call and amount and marks it settled with the settle cdmHash.
Contract transfers the released tokens back to the pledgor.
Each gateway pushes the Returned and CallSettled events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; each service folds the settle step and updates its balance.

flows.name: Default and enforcement
flows.description: After a pledgor default, the secured party enforces against the pledged initial margin. There is no direct service-to-service channel; the pledgor learns of the default from the on-chain feed through its own gateway.

transitions.description: Secured party declares a pledgor default in its console.
Console submits the default declaration to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service forwards the default notice to the oracle service.
Oracle publishes the default status through the operator's gateway.
Operator's gateway writes the default to the feed; the secured party's gateway then submits enforce() with the secured party key.
Contract confirms the default status.
Contract transfers the pledged tokens to the secured party.
Each gateway pushes the DefaultPublished and Enforced events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; the pledgor's service records the default and each service records the enforcement.

flows.name: Close-out netting on default
flows.description: After a pledgor default the secured party, as the Non-defaulting Party, closes out the netting set under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement Section 6(e) (cdm-ext CloseOutNetting, gap G15): the Early Termination Amount is netted, the pledged initial margin is applied to it under the security interest, and the surplus goes back to the pledgor. The CDM CloseOutStatement is carried off-chain and anchored by its hash.

transitions.description: Secured party enters the Close-out Amount of the netting set and closes out in its console.
Console submits the close-out to the secured party's workflow service.
If the oracle feed does not show the default yet, the service sends the default notice to the oracle service.
Oracle publishes the default status through the operator's gateway.
Service values the escrow after haircuts at the feed prices, builds the CDM CloseOutStatement and publishes it to the payload store, readable by both parties.
Service submits closeOut with the Early Termination Amount owed and the statement hash; the gateway signs with the secured party key.
Contract confirms the pledgor's default on the feed and reads the prices.
Contract applies whole units of pledged tokens, in the order first pledged, until the amount owed is covered, transfers them to the secured party and returns the rest to the pledgor.
Each gateway pushes the ClosedOut event to its own workflow service; the pledgor's service fetches the statement by its hash, recomputes it with CloseOutNetting and records it.

flows.name: Substitution of pledged collateral
flows.description: The pledgor substitutes part of its pledged initial margin under ISDA CSA Paragraph 4(d) (cdm-ext Create_CollateralSubstitution, gap G16, defect D5): it gives notice, the secured party consents (the agreement elects consent, Paragraph 13 (f)(ii)), and on settlement the substitute enters escrow and the original items return in one transaction. Each step's CDM SubstitutionInstruction is carried off-chain and anchored by its hash.

transitions.description: Pledgor chooses the pledged items to return and the substitute in its console.
Console submits the request to the pledgor's workflow service.
Service values both sides after haircuts at the feed prices and publishes the CDM SubstitutionInstruction (request) to the payload store.
Service submits requestSubstitution; the contract checks the originals are in escrow and the substitute is eligible and worth at least as much.
Secured party sees the request in its console and consents or refuses.
Console submits the decision to the secured party's workflow service.
Service publishes the CDM SubstitutionInstruction (consent) to the payload store.
Service submits decideSubstitution, signed with the secured party key.
Pledgor settles the consented substitution in its console.
Pledgor's service publishes the CDM SubstitutionInstruction (settle) and submits settleSubstitution; the gateway approves the substitute first.
Contract checks the values again at the current feed prices, moves the substitute into escrow and returns the original items to the pledgor.

Each gateway pushes the substitution events to its own workflow service; each service folds the three CDM steps through Create_CollateralSubstitution with the escrow it reads at the block before each step, and both reach the same state.

flows.name: Interest on cash collateral
flows.description: The secured party pays the pledgor interest on its cash collateral (tUSD) for one Interest Period under the CSA's interest elections (cdm-ext Create_CollateralInterestStatement on CDM CollateralInterestParameters, gap G17). Interim reduction: every day of the period has the cash now in escrow and one observed rate (task-sme-interest-daily-balances). The CDM CollateralInterestStatement is carried off-chain and anchored by its hash; a negative amount is paid by the pledgor.

transitions.description: Secured party enters the Interest Period and the observed rate and states the interest in its console.
Console submits the period and rate to the secured party's workflow service.
Service reads the pledgor's tUSD in escrow through its gateway.
Service builds the CDM CollateralInterestStatement (daily accrual at ACT/360, rounded to whole USD, Transfer handling) and publishes it to the payload store, readable by both parties.
Service submits stateInterest with the transfer amount and the statement hash; the gateway approves the control contract for the tUSD and signs with the secured party key.
Contract checks the cash token is eligible with no haircut and, for a positive amount, transfers the tUSD from the secured party to the pledgor.
Each gateway pushes the InterestStated and InterestSettled events to its own workflow service.
The pledgor's service fetches the statement by its on-chain hash, recomputes it from its days and records it.
Both consoles list the statement as paid and verified; for a negative amount the pledgor pays it from its console (payInterest).

flows.name: Settlement netting of collateral movements
flows.description: The day's agreed VM calls, VM returns and Interest Amounts held for netting between the two parties settle by one transfer of tUSD from the party that owes the net (task-csa-settlement-netting; the project owner's scope of 2026-11-06). cdm-ext Create_SettlementNetting nets the CDM SettlementObligations under the agreement's netInterestWithMarginCalls election; the SettlementNettingStatement and each call's SettleCall step (naming the netting) are carried off-chain and anchored by their hashes. Initial margin does not net. The rules are assumptions awaiting task-sme-settlement-netting-rules.

transitions.description: The party owing the net (here the pledgor) sees the movements that can net and the net in its console, and settles them.
Console asks the party's workflow service to settle every movement that can net now.
Service reads the agreed VM calls with an accepted tUSD proposal, the agreed return calls and the held Interest Amounts between the two parties.
Service builds the CDM SettlementNettingStatement (Create_SettlementNetting) and one SettleCall step per call naming the netting, and publishes them to the payload store.
Service submits settleNetted with the hashes; the gateway approves the net in tUSD and the contract checks each movement, marks the calls and interest settled, and transfers the net once.
Each gateway pushes SettlementNetted and the CallSettled steps; both services fetch the statement by its hash and verify it against the chain, and both consoles show the netting.

flows.name: Collateral allocation (suggested basket)
flows.description: The called party of an agreed IM or VM call asks its workflow service for a basket that covers the agreed amount (task-csa-allocation; the project owner's scope of 2026-11-07, wp-adr-allocation-scope). cdm-ext AllocateCollateral takes the party's eligible holdings in its ranking order (registry order by default) and rounds the last one up to whole units; concentration limits are not applied. Nothing is recorded: the party edits or keeps the basket and proposes it through the existing proposal step (flow-im-margin-call-pledge, flow-vm-margin-call-transfer). The default ranking awaits task-sme-allocation-ranking.

transitions.description: The pledgor asks for a suggested allocation on an agreed call in its console.
Console asks the party's workflow service for an allocation of the call, with an optional ranking.
Service reads the call, the party's token balances, the oracle feed prices and the pair's eligibility and haircuts through its own gateway.
The console fills the proposal basket from the service's CDM AllocateCollateral result; the pledgor proposes it as before.

flows.name: Reconciliation (trade portfolios and records against the ledger)
flows.description: Either party reconciles (task-csa-reconciliation, gap G35; the project owner's scope of 2026-11-07, wp-adr-reconciliation-scope). Trade portfolios: each party's workflow service holds CDM sample TradeStates and its own valuation of each; the initiating party sends its PortfolioSnapshot to the counterparty's service, each commits its snapshot hash on-chain, and both run cdm-ext ReconcilePortfolios (trades matched by UTI on key economic terms and a valuation tolerance, with each party's exposure) and commit the result hash; the run is Agreed on-chain when the hashes match. The called party can dispute an issued call citing the run's breaks (a CDM Dispute, G3). Records against the ledger: cdm-ext ReconcileWithLedger compares the status, called and agreed amounts in the party's stored MarginCallStates with the contract's, and the pledgor's escrow by token as the party's settled records build it (initial margin deliveries, returns that released initial margin, substitutions, since the pair's last enforcement or close-out) with the control contract's escrow. Key terms, tolerance and cadence await task-sme-reconciliation-rules.

transitions.description: The pledgor asks its console to reconcile its trade portfolio with the secured party's.
Console asks the party's workflow service to reconcile portfolios.
Service builds its CDM PortfolioSnapshot and commits its hash to the portfolio reconciliation contract through its own gateway.

Service sends the snapshot to the counterparty's service, which checks it against the committed hash, commits its own snapshot and result hashes through its own gateway, and answers with its snapshot.
Service checks the counterparty's snapshot against its committed hash, runs ReconcilePortfolios and commits the result hash; the contract records the run as Agreed when both hashes match.
The console shows the breaks, the two exposures and the on-chain agreement; on an issued call the pledgor disputes citing the run (respond step, a CDM Dispute recorded with the call).
Console asks the party's service to reconcile its records with the ledger.
Service reads its stored CDM MarginCallStates of the pair's calls and its settled substitutions, and builds the pledgor's escrow by token from them.

Service reads the pair's calls from the margin call contract, the escrow from the control contract and the last enforcement or close-out from the settlement history, and runs ReconcileWithLedger on the two sets of facts.

flows.name: Amendment of agreement terms
flows.description: Either party proposes an amendment of the IM CSA's terms: a new Minimum Transfer Amount through CDM's Create_AgreementEvent (intent AmendedTerms, qualified AgreementTermsChange by cdm-ext) and haircut changes to the eligibility schedule (cdm-ext Create_CollateralAgreementAmendment). The baseline agreement is CDM's published sample 2018 NY law IM CSA. The CDM CollateralAgreementAmendment is carried off-chain and anchored by its hash, chained from the pair's current agreement hash; the other party consents on-chain, the contract applies the haircuts to the pair, and both services fold the agreed amendments to the same terms.

transitions.description: One party (here the secured party) enters a new pledgor MTA and a token's haircut and proposes the amendment in its console.
Console submits the amendment to the party's workflow service.
Service builds the CDM CollateralAgreementAmendment over the terms in force (folded from the agreed amendments) and publishes it to the payload store, readable by both parties.
Service submits proposeAmendment with the haircut terms, the pair's current agreement hash (beforeHash) and the amendment hash; the contract accepts one pending amendment per pair.
Each gateway pushes the AmendmentProposed event to its own workflow service; both consoles list the proposal.

The other party (here the pledgor) consents in its console; its service fetches the amendment by its on-chain hash, verifies it against the terms in force and checks the on-chain haircut terms are the document's changes.

Service publishes its decision document and submits decideAmendment; on consent the contract copies the global schedule for the pair on its first amendment, applies the haircut terms and sets the pair's agreement hash to the amendment hash.
Each gateway pushes AmendmentDecided; both services fold the agreed amendments, read the pair's haircuts from the contract, and value collateral and revalue with the amended MTA and haircuts.

flows.name: Margin call cancellation
flows.description: The calling party withdraws a margin call the called party has not answered; once the call is answered and not settled (wholly disputed calls included), either party requests its cancellation and the other accepts or refuses (ISO 20022 colr.005 and colr.006). An accepted cancellation voids any proposal not yet delivered; no collateral has moved, since collateral moves only at settlement. Each step is a cdm-ext MarginCallInstruction (WithdrawCall, RequestCancellation, DecideCancellation) anchored by its hash and folded by both services to the Cancelled status. The rules are the project owner's assumptions, to be confirmed in task-sme-call-cancellation-rules.

transitions.description: The calling party (here the secured party) withdraws an unanswered call, or requests the cancellation of an answered one, with a reason, in its console.
Console submits the withdrawal or request to the party's workflow service.
Service builds the CDM step (WithdrawCall or RequestCancellation) and publishes it to the payload store, readable by both parties.

Service submits withdrawCall (caller, unanswered call) or requestCancellation (either party, answered call not settled) with the step hash; while a request is pending the contract takes no proposal, decision or settlement on the call.
Each gateway pushes the CallWithdrawn or CancellationRequested step to its own workflow service; both consoles show the call cancelled, or the pending request.
The other party (here the pledgor) accepts or refuses the request in its console.

Its service publishes the DecideCancellation step and submits decideCancellation; on acceptance the contract sets the call Cancelled and voids a proposal not yet delivered, on refusal the call continues where it was.
Each gateway pushes CancellationDecided; both services fold the call's steps to the same MarginCallState (Cancelled, qualifier MarginCallCancelled) with a complete ledger anchor per step.

flows.name: Replacement of a cancelled margin call
flows.description: The calling party issues a corrected call that replaces a call it cancelled (flow-call-cancellation). The new call keeps the cancelled call's kind and called party; its cdm-ext IssueCall step names the cancelled call (replacesCall), and the contract links the two calls both ways, one replacement per cancelled call. The rules are assumptions to be confirmed in task-sme-call-cancellation-rules (question 5).

transitions.description: The calling party (here the secured party) enters the corrected amount on its cancelled call and issues the replacement in its console.
Console submits the replacement (the cancelled call's id and the amount) to the party's workflow service.
Service reads the cancelled call from the chain: the party called it, it is cancelled and has no replacement yet.
Service builds the IssueCall step naming the cancelled call, checks it against the cancelled call's folded CDM state (ReplacementAllowed), and publishes it to the payload store.

Service submits issueReplacementCall with the step hash; the contract checks the cancelled call (same caller, called party and kind, no replacement yet), issues the new call and emits CallIssued and CallReplaced.
Each gateway pushes the new call; both consoles show the link (replaces / replaced by), and the called party answers the new call as any other.
